what: Behind the fixed header bar, eight layers with different blur strengths (.5·3·8·12·15·32·64·100px) are joined with band-shaped masks, so content passing below blurs more and more toward the top of the header, spreading like fog. While the Hero is more than 15% visible the blur panel stays pulled up, and when it leaves it comes down in .4s

options.hero: Hero (selector) that clears the blur — without it, it stays blurred
options.threshold: Lifts when this much of the Hero is visible, default .15
options.dur: Duration of descending and clearing (s), default .4
options.height: Blur panel height (relative to the headline), default 130%

use: <header data-fx="blur-stack-header" data-fx-blur-stack-header="hero: .hero" style="position: fixed; top: 0; width: 100%">
note: /  backdrop-filter is used in eight layers, so it costs a lot of GPU when the header is wide and the content below is a photo. The header itself must be fixed (position: fixed · sticky) so the blur passes over the content

from.where: shared.css .su-header__blur (original l-header__gradient-blur — eight-layer blur, once 15% of the hero is visible it slides translateY(-100%) in .4s cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1))
